decision_nodes.title: Back Pain Hub - Sick Check First
decision_nodes.body:
Open first:
- [Hub Steps Summary](#/info/bp-steps)
- [Hub Stop / Pitfalls](#/info/bp-stop)

**First 60 seconds:**
- General appearance: pale, diaphoretic, unable to sit still, toxic, septic, severe distress?
- Vitals trend: hypotension, fever, tachycardia, hypoxia.
- Neuro: leg strength, sensation, reflexes, gait if safe, saddle sensation, bowel/bladder symptoms.
- Vascular/abdominal: abdominal pain, pulsatile mass, syncope, unequal pulses, tearing pain.
- Infection risk: IVDU, diabetes, immunosuppression, recent bacteremia, dialysis, spinal injection/procedure, indwelling catheter.
- Fracture/cancer risk: trauma, osteoporosis, steroids, age, malignancy, weight loss, night pain.

Most back pain is mechanical. The ED job is to rapidly find the few that are spine, vascular, infectious, renal, traumatic, or malignant emergencies.
decision_nodes.summary: Vitals, neuro/bowel/bladder, vascular/abdominal, infection, trauma, cancer risk first.

decision_nodes.title: Time-Critical Exclusions - Pick the Best Fit
decision_nodes.body: Choose the first dangerous lane. Do not start with "sciatica" until these are screened.

options.label: Urinary retention/incontinence, saddle symptoms, bilateral sciatica, progressive leg weakness
Fever, IVDU, diabetes, immunosuppression, recent bacteremia/procedure, focal spine tenderness
Older vascular risk, abrupt severe back/abdominal pain, syncope, hypotension, pulse deficit
Trauma, osteoporosis, chronic steroids, cancer, weight loss, night pain
Flank pain, fever, urinary symptoms, stone-like colic, solitary kidney, pregnancy
Unilateral radicular pain, positive straight-leg, no red flags, normal strength/bladder
No immediate exclusion hit
options.description: Initial back pain bundle and reassess

decision_nodes.summary: Cauda, spine infection, AAA/dissection, fracture/cancer, renal mimics, and radiculopathy are the main lanes.

decision_nodes.title: Cauda Equina / Conus Medullaris
decision_nodes.body:
Open [Cauda Equina Syndrome](#/tree/cauda-equina).

**Next 5 minutes:** bladder scan/PVR, focused sacral exam when feasible, leg motor/reflex/sensation exam, urgent MRI lumbar spine, early spine/neurosurgery call if symptoms fit.

**Red flags:** urinary retention or new overflow incontinence, saddle anesthesia, bilateral sciatica, progressive bilateral leg weakness, fecal incontinence, severe neurologic deficit.

**Pitfall:** pain may be improving while bladder/neurologic injury is worsening. Do not reassure based on pain response.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Suspected cauda equina needs emergency MRI and spine pathway.

decision_nodes.title: Spinal Epidural Abscess / Vertebral Osteomyelitis
decision_nodes.body:
Open [Low Back Pain Decision Support](#/tree/low-back-pain) while using spine infection posture.

**Next 5 minutes:** neuro exam, ESR/CRP, blood cultures when febrile/high suspicion, MRI spine with and without contrast; consider whole-spine MRI when symptoms do not localize or risk is high. Antibiotics after cultures when stable; do not delay antibiotics for sepsis or neurologic deficit.

**Pitfall:** the classic triad is insensitive. No fever does not clear SEA.
decision_nodes.recommendation: MRI is the key diagnostic test when spine infection is plausible.

decision_nodes.title: AAA / Aortic Dissection Back-Pain Variant
decision_nodes.body:
Open [Aortic Aneurysm ED Management](#/tree/aortic-aneurysm) or [Aortic Dissection](#/tree/aortic-dissection).

**Next 5 minutes:** two large-bore IVs, type/screen or MTP posture if unstable, bedside aorta ultrasound if rapid and available, CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis when stable, vascular/cardiothoracic surgery early. For dissection, impulse control before vasodilator when perfusing.

**Pitfall:** do not anchor on musculoskeletal pain in an older vascular-risk patient with syncope, hypotension, abdominal pain, pulse deficit, or abrupt maximal pain.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Vascular back pain is a resuscitation diagnosis. Image and consult early.

decision_nodes.title: Fracture / Malignancy / Metastatic Cord Compression
decision_nodes.body:
Open [Low Back Pain Decision Support](#/tree/low-back-pain).

**Next 5 minutes:** neuro exam, pain control, CT or radiographs for trauma/fracture by risk, MRI when cancer with neurologic symptoms, severe progressive pain, suspected cord/cauda compression, or epidural disease. Consider steroids after specialist discussion when metastatic cord compression is suspected.

**Pitfall:** new severe back pain in a cancer patient is malignant spinal disease until reasonably excluded.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Cancer, fracture risk, or neuro findings should trigger imaging beyond routine mechanical back pain care.

decision_nodes.title: Renal / Urinary / Intra-Abdominal Mimic
decision_nodes.body:
Open [Adult UTI](#/tree/adult-uti) or [Urinary Retention](#/tree/urinary-retention) when those fit.

**Next 5 minutes:** UA, pregnancy test when applicable, renal function, bedside bladder scan if retention, CT/ultrasound strategy for stone/obstruction/pyelo complication by risk. Reconsider abdominal pathology when pain is not reproducible/mechanical or vitals are abnormal.

**Pitfall:** flank/back pain plus fever, solitary kidney, AKI, pregnancy, uncontrolled pain/vomiting, or sepsis physiology is not simple outpatient back pain.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Treat renal/urinary mimics by obstruction, infection severity, pregnancy, and renal risk.

decision_nodes.title: Radiculopathy / Mechanical Pattern
decision_nodes.body:
Open [Low Back Pain Decision Support](#/tree/low-back-pain).

**Next 5 minutes:** confirm no red flags, document motor/reflex/sensation, treat pain to enable mobility, avoid routine advanced imaging for uncomplicated acute low back pain/radiculopathy, encourage activity as tolerated.

**Pitfall:** radicular pain does not equal cauda equina. Cauda requires bowel/bladder/saddle/progressive bilateral weakness screening every time.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Mechanical/radicular pain can be outpatient only after red flags and function are reassessed.

decision_nodes.title: Rescue / Initial Bundle + Reassess
decision_nodes.body:
**Default bundle when no killer has declared itself:**
- Analgesia: acetaminophen, NSAID if safe, topical/local measures, muscle relaxer selectively; avoid routine opioids when alternatives work.
- Neuro exam before and after analgesia: gait, strength, reflexes, sensation.
- Bladder scan/PVR when urinary symptoms, severe bilateral symptoms, or cauda concern.
- ESR/CRP when infection risk exists; normal labs do not overrule high clinical suspicion.
- Encourage movement as tolerated; avoid prolonged bedrest instructions for uncomplicated mechanical pain.

**Reassess in 30-60 minutes:** ability to stand/walk, neuro exam, bladder symptoms, pain control, vitals.
decision_nodes.summary: Analgesia, repeat neuro/gait, PVR when indicated, ESR/CRP by infection risk, then reassess.

decision_nodes.title: Reassess After Initial Bundle
decision_nodes.body: Disposition depends on function and the repeat neurologic exam.

options.label: Worse, cannot walk, new neuro/bladder/fever/vascular feature
Persistent severe pain or red-flag uncertainty
Improved, ambulatory, no red flags, stable exam

decision_nodes.summary: New neuro/bladder/fever/vascular features reset the workup.

decision_nodes.title: Imaging Decision
decision_nodes.body:
**Image by suspected emergency:**
- **MRI lumbar spine:** cauda/conus, progressive neurologic deficit, suspected epidural abscess/vertebral osteomyelitis, malignancy with neuro signs, cord/cauda compression.
- **MRI with contrast / whole spine:** infection, malignancy, nonlocalizing spinal infection symptoms.
- **CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis:** aortic dissection or unstable vascular back-pain phenotype when stable enough.
- **Bedside aorta ultrasound:** rapid screen for AAA in older vascular-risk patients; do not let a limited scan delay CTA/surgery when unstable.
- **CT/radiographs:** trauma or compression fracture risk.
- **No routine imaging:** uncomplicated acute low back pain or radiculopathy without red flags.

Image because the result changes management, not because the pain is severe.
decision_nodes.summary: MRI for cauda/infection/cancer/neuro, CTA/US for aorta, CT/XR for fracture, no imaging for uncomplicated mechanical pain.

decision_nodes.title: Disposition
decision_nodes.body: Disposition follows neurologic safety, infection/vascular risk, mobility, and pain control.

options.label: Persistent severe pain, equivocal red flags, pending MRI/CTA/labs
Mechanical pattern, ambulatory, no red flags, safe follow-up

decision_nodes.summary: Danger signs admit; uncertainty observes; uncomplicated mechanical pain discharges after function and red flags are checked.

decision_nodes.title: Admit / Transfer / Specialty Pathway
decision_nodes.body: Admit/transfer for cauda/conus symptoms, progressive neurologic deficit, suspected or confirmed SEA/NVO, sepsis, AAA/dissection, unstable vitals, fracture needing intervention, malignancy/cord compression concern, inability to ambulate safely, urinary retention with neurologic concern, or pain requiring inpatient control.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Admit or transfer when the diagnosis threatens neurologic function, vascular survival, infection control, or safe mobility.

decision_nodes.title: Observation / Serial Exam
decision_nodes.body: Observe when MRI/CTA/labs are pending, pain prevents a reliable exam or ambulation test, symptoms are evolving, infection risk is moderate with unclear labs, or social support/transport is unsafe after treatment.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Observation is for serial neuro/gait/vitals and completion of targeted testing.

decision_nodes.title: Discharge Checklist
decision_nodes.body:
Discharge only when: no red flags, normal or baseline neuro exam, no bowel/bladder/saddle symptoms, ambulatory or baseline mobility restored, pain controlled enough for function, no infection/vascular/trauma/cancer concern, and follow-up is realistic.

**Return precautions:** urinary retention/incontinence, saddle numbness, leg weakness, inability to walk, fever, worsening severe pain, abdominal pain/syncope, new numbness, cancer red flags, or uncontrolled vomiting/pain.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Document red-flag screen, repeat neuro/gait exam, and explicit cauda/infection/vascular return precautions.
